effects: Pulls `amount` T from the signer into the RebateStaking contract (token.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount)).
Raises the signer's stakedAmount by `amount`, which raises their fee-rebate cap (stakedAmount / rebatePerToken).
If the signer was another staker's delegatee, that delegation is cleared, so the signer stops using the other staker's rebate capacity (delegates[msg.sender] = 0).
formats.shown: "Stake T" with the amount in T at 18 decimals, e.g. "1000T".

findings.title: stake: if the signer was another staker's delegatee, staking silently ends that delegation.
findings.evidence: RebateStaking.sol stake(): `address otherStaker = delegates[msg.sender]; if (otherStaker != address(0)) { stakes[otherStaker].delegatee = address(0); delegates[msg.sender] = address(0); ... }`. Descriptor intent is only "Stake T" and the screen has nothing about delegation.
findings.fix: Add a short note to the intent, e.g. "Stake T (ends any rebate delegation to you)", or describe it in the descriptor's documentation.

findings.title: stake: amount uses a `unit` with base "T" rather than tokenAmount tied to the T token address.
findings.evidence: descriptor stake field: `"format": "unit", "params": {"base": "T", "decimals": 18}`. The token is set at initialize to 0xCdF7028ceAB81fA0C6971208e83fa7872994beE5 (proxy constructor _data). The screen shows "1000T" with no space and no link to the token.
findings.fix: Use `tokenAmount` with `token` set to the T address so the wallet shows the verified ticker and decimals.

effects: Marks `amount` of the signer's stake as unstaking and starts the unstaking timer (unstakingTimestamp = now). No tokens move.
The signer's rebate cap drops at once, because it is computed from stakedAmount - unstakingAmount.
The tokens can be withdrawn only after unstakingPeriod (set to 30 days at initialization; it lives in storage), and only one unstaking can run at a time.
formats.shown: "Start unstaking T" with the amount in T.

findings.title: startUnstaking: the lock period and the immediate drop in rebate cap are not shown.
findings.evidence: RebateStaking.sol startUnstaking() sets unstakingTimestamp. finalizeUnstaking() requires `unstakingTimestamp + unstakingPeriod <= block.timestamp`. getRebateCap uses `stakedAmount - unstakingAmount`. unstakingPeriod is a storage value (0x278d00 = 30 days at init).
findings.fix: Optionally say in the intent that tokens unlock after the unstaking period and stop counting toward rebates now.

effects: Sends the signer's pending unstakingAmount of T from the staking contract to `receiver`, which can be any address.
Lowers the signer's stakedAmount by that amount and resets the unstaking state.
If the signer's stake reaches zero, their rebate delegatee is cleared.
formats.shown: "Finalize T unstaking" with the Receiver address.

findings.title: finalizeUnstaking: the T amount sent to the receiver comes from storage and is not shown.
findings.evidence: RebateStaking.sol finalizeUnstaking(): `uint96 amount = stakeInfo.unstakingAmount; ... token.safeTransfer(receiver, amount);`. The calldata carries only `receiver`.
findings.fix: None possible from calldata; the descriptor could mention 'the amount you started unstaking' in the intent.

findings.title: finalizeUnstaking: the intent does not say that T is sent to the receiver, which may be a third party.
findings.evidence: descriptor intent "Finalize T unstaking". There is no interpolatedIntent; the receiver appears only as a field. Code: `token.safeTransfer(receiver, amount)`.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Withdraw unstaked T to {receiver}".

effects: Lets `_delegatee` use the signer's fee-rebate capacity on tBTC bridge fees (delegates[_delegatee] = msg.sender; the bridge's applyForRebate maps the user to the staker).
Removes any previous delegatee's access to the signer's rebate.
Passing the zero address or the signer's own address clears delegation instead of setting it.
formats.shown: "Set rebate delegatee" with the Delegatee address.

findings.title: setDelegatee: zero address or own address means 'remove delegatee', but it is shown literally.
findings.evidence: RebateStaking.sol setDelegatee(): `if (_delegatee == address(0) || _delegatee == msg.sender) { stakeInfo.delegatee = address(0); ... return; }`. The descriptor shows only the Delegatee address, so 0x000…0 would appear as if it were being set as delegatee.
findings.fix: Note in the label or intent that the zero address or your own address clears the delegatee.

findings.title: setDelegatee: the intent does not say the delegatee consumes the signer's rebate capacity.
findings.evidence: getStaker()/applyForRebate(): fees the delegatee pays use stakes[staker] rebates. The intent says only "Set rebate delegatee".
findings.fix: e.g. "Let {_delegatee} use your T stake's fee rebates".

effects: Sets which tBTC bridge fees (deposits, redemptions or both) the signer's stake rebates. This also applies to their delegatee's use. No assets move.
formats.shown: "Set fee waiver mode" with the mode name (Mint and redeem / Deposits only / Redemptions only).

findings.title: setRebateTreasuryFeeMode: wording is inconsistent ('fee waiver' vs 'rebate', 'Mint' vs 'Deposits').
findings.evidence: descriptor enums: `"0": "Mint and redeem", "1": "Deposits only"`. Intent "Set fee waiver mode" while setDelegatee says "rebate". The code's enum is Both/DepositOnly/RedemptionOnly. The values match the code.
findings.fix: Use one term throughout, e.g. "Deposits and redemptions" and "Set fee rebate mode".

stake(uint96 amount).worst: stake: if the signer was another staker's delegatee, staking silently ends that delegation.

setDelegatee(address _delegatee).worst: setDelegatee: zero address or own address means 'remove delegatee', but it is shown literally.
